analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts (lines 859-1413) were supplied, and these cover documentation only. No code, configuration or mode changes were visible in these units. The changelog entries describe security-relevant behaviour but do not change it.

Relevant threat IDs touched by the prose:
- T-053, T-054, T-052, T-057 and TB-011, TB-009: App Attest serving, qualified signed code, revocation and fencing of queued requests, and the 'off by default' rollout posture at lines 860-864.
- T-041 and TB-007: the prefix-cache and SSD checkpoint changes at lines 1039-1040, 1068, 1084, 1123 and 1259-1272. The accepted-risk and SEC-035 posture appears consistent with these entries, and the entries claim tenant, model and prompt identity gates are preserved. The disk budget described at line 1123 and the 20 GiB reserve match T-041's description. Line 1257 shows the older 100 GiB ceiling as historical, which the later 0.9.1 entry (line 1123) supersedes.

I saw nothing in these units that widens the at-rest surface, loosens the 30-minute TTL, or weakens account-scoped cacheSalt. The changelog states the claims but gives no evidence of the underlying code. The actual implementation files (SSDPrefixCache, SSDBlockStore, coordinator cache_route_keys.go and the App Attest code) were not in this batch. Integration should check any accompanying code changes against T-041, T-053 and T-054 and the changelog claims; none of the changelog statements should be treated as verified. No new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption is visible from the changelog text alone.
